topic: Annual Cycle of Jhum Shifting Cultivation
questionText:
Arrange the agricultural operations of traditional Jhum (shifting cultivation) in correct chronological sequence throughout the annual cycle:
(A) Slashing of natural forest undergrowth and trees on hill slopes during the dry winter (December–February)
(B) Controlled burning of dried vegetation and debris to create nutrient-rich wood ash (March–April)
(C) Dibbling mixed seeds (millets, upland rice, pulses, vegetables) with digging sticks upon the first monsoon showers (May–June)
(D) Harvesting of diverse staggered crops in succession and leaving the plot fallow for 5–10 years for forest regeneration (October–December)

Choose the correct chronological/logical sequence from the options given below:

options.text: A, B, C, D
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

options.text: B, A, C, D
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A, C, B, D
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
The Jhum cycle proceeds: Clearing/slashing -> Controlled burning -> Sowing/dibbling with rain -> Staggered harvesting and fallowing.
Hence Option B is correct.
Hence, option (A) is correct.
